title: Pegula Saves Match Point to Reach the Last Four
summary:
Jessica Pegula saved a match point and fought into the last four of the WTA Finals. She beat Linda Noskova 7-6, 4-6, 7-5 in a match that went back and forth.

Pegula had to win. Coco Gauff had beaten Marta Kostyuk earlier on Thursday, so only a win over Noskova would carry her through.

Noskova went ahead in the third set and had a match point at 5-4 on Pegula's serve. But she could not take it, and Pegula held on to win.

Pegula's serve was the star of the show. She hit 16 aces, the most she has ever hit in a WTA Tour match. Noskova had trouble with her own serve, hitting 15 double faults.

Noskova had already made the semi-finals, where she will face Elina Svitolina or Aryna Sabalenka on Saturday. Pegula will play French Open champion Mirra Andreeva next.

Earlier, Gauff also fought back to beat Kostyuk, even after treatment on her lower back and going 5-1 down in the second set.
why_it_matters: Saving a match point shows that you should never give up, even when you are one point from losing, which is a lesson for any game you play.
